about: One entry per X-ray model. Coordinates are three.js (y up, metres). Every model stands on the floor at the origin with its front toward +z. 'body' is the tank body or the furnace cabinet used for photo fitting (pipes, vents and extras left out). 'match' says which photo analyses a model may be drawn over; anything else gets the typical (generic) experience or none.

gas_tank_water_heater.title: Gas water heater
gas_tank_water_heater.typical: a typical gas tank water heater

heat.say: The burner lights under the tank. Heat rises through the flue in the middle and warms the water around it.

lessons.label: The anode rod
lessons.say: The anode rod is a sacrificial metal rod. Over the years it slowly gets eaten away so your tank does not rust.

lessons.label: Sediment
lessons.say: Minerals in the water settle at the bottom of the tank as sediment. Too much makes the heater rumble and work harder.

outer_jacket: The painted metal skin you see in your home. It protects the foam insulation underneath.
insulation: A layer of foam that keeps the hot water hot, like a thermos.
inner_tank: The glass-lined steel tank that holds the water, usually 40 or 50 gallons.
water_volume: Hot water rises to the top where it leaves for your faucets. Cold water sinks to the bottom.
dip_tube: A plastic tube that carries new cold water down to the bottom of the tank, so it does not mix with the hot water on top.
anode_rod: A sacrificial metal rod. It slowly corrodes so the steel tank does not. It wears out over the years.
burner: Gas burns here, under the tank, like a stove burner turned upside down.
burner_flame: A healthy flame is blue and steady.
pilot_assembly: A small flame that lights the burner whenever the water needs heat.
gas_control_valve: The knob on the front. It sets the water temperature and turns the burner on when the tank cools down.
flue: A pipe up the middle of the tank. Hot exhaust from the burner passes through it and warms the water on the way.
flue_baffle: A twisted metal strip in the flue. It slows the hot exhaust down so more heat goes into the water.
draft_hood: The cone on top where exhaust leaves the heater and heads up the vent.
vent_pipe: Carries the burner's exhaust safely outside.
combustion_chamber: The space under the tank where the burner fires.
tp_relief_valve: Opens by itself if the tank ever gets too hot or the pressure too high. An important safety part.
drain_valve: Used to flush sediment out of the bottom of the tank.
cold_water_inlet: Where cold water from your home's supply comes in.
hot_water_outlet: Where hot water leaves for your sinks, showers and appliances.
sediment: Minerals that settle at the bottom of the tank over time.
air_intake: The burner breathes in air here. Keep it clear of boxes and lint.
data_plate: Lists the model, size and age of the heater.
gas_shutoff_valve: The valve that turns gas off to the heater.

electric_tank_water_heater.title: Electric water heater
electric_tank_water_heater.typical: a typical electric tank water heater

heat.say: Electric heating elements reach into the water, like the coil in a kettle. The lower one does most of the work.

lessons.label: The anode rod
lessons.say: The anode rod is a sacrificial metal rod. Over the years it slowly gets eaten away so your tank does not rust.

lessons.label: Sediment
lessons.say: Minerals in the water settle at the bottom of the tank as sediment. It can bury the lower heating element and make it fail early.

outer_jacket: The painted metal skin you see in your home. It protects the foam insulation underneath.
insulation: A layer of foam that keeps the hot water hot, like a thermos.
inner_tank: The glass-lined steel tank that holds the water, usually 40 or 50 gallons.
water_volume: Hot water rises to the top where it leaves for your faucets. Cold water sinks to the bottom.
dip_tube: A plastic tube that carries new cold water down to the bottom of the tank, so it does not mix with the hot water on top.
anode_rod: A sacrificial metal rod. It slowly corrodes so the steel tank does not. It wears out over the years.
upper_heating_element: Heats the top of the tank first so you get hot water sooner.
lower_heating_element: Does most of the heating, like the coil in a kettle.
lower_element_glow: Does most of the heating, like the coil in a kettle.
upper_thermostat: Senses the water temperature and decides when the elements turn on.
high_limit_control: A safety switch that shuts the power off if the water ever gets too hot.
electrical_junction_box: Where your home's electric line connects to the heater.
tp_relief_valve: Opens by itself if the tank ever gets too hot or the pressure too high. An important safety part.
drain_valve: Used to flush sediment out of the bottom of the tank.
cold_water_inlet: Where cold water from your home's supply comes in.
hot_water_outlet: Where hot water leaves for your sinks, showers and appliances.
sediment: Minerals that settle at the bottom of the tank over time.
data_plate: Lists the model, size and age of the heater.
upper_access_panel: A cover over the upper thermostat and element. Only a trained person should open it: there is live electricity behind it.
lower_access_panel: A cover over the lower thermostat and element. Only a trained person should open it: there is live electricity behind it.

heat.say: The thermostat calls for heat. A small fan clears the burner box, the igniter glows and the burners light. The flames heat the metal heat exchanger, and the big blower pushes your home's air across it and out the vents, warm. The fire and the air you breathe never touch.

lessons.label: Air conditioning
lessons.say: In summer the same blower pushes air through the cold coil on top. The coil pulls heat and moisture out of the air, and the water drips into a pan and drains away.

lessons.label: The filter
lessons.say: The filter catches dust before it reaches the blower and the coil. A clogged filter starves the system of air, so it runs longer and wears out sooner. Check it every month or two.

lessons.label: Heat exchanger
lessons.say: The heat exchanger keeps the flames and their exhaust apart from the air you breathe. Your technician checks it for cracks, because a crack could let exhaust into the airflow.

cabinet: The metal box of the furnace. Everything that heats and moves your air is inside.
blower_door: The lower front door. It covers the blower and the control board. The furnace shuts off when it is open.
burner_door: The upper front door, over the burners. Keep it on: the burners need it closed to get their air right.
door_switch: A safety switch. It cuts the power when the blower door comes off.
data_plate: Lists the model, size and age of the furnace.
gas_valve: Opens to send gas to the burners when the thermostat calls for heat.
gas_pipe: Brings natural gas or propane to the furnace.
drip_leg: A short capped pipe that catches dirt and moisture before they reach the gas valve.
burner_assembly: Where the gas burns, in a row of small burners.
flames: Healthy flames are blue and steady.
igniter: Glows red hot to light the gas. It replaced the old standing pilot light.
igniter_glow: Glows red hot to light the gas. It replaced the old standing pilot light.
flame_sensor: Proves the flame lit. If it does not see a flame, it shuts the gas off. A dirty one is a common no-heat call.
heat_exchanger: Metal tubes the flames heat from inside. Your air warms on the outside of them and never touches the fire.
inducer: A small fan that pulls the exhaust through the heat exchanger and pushes it up the vent.
pressure_switch: Checks that the draft inducer is moving the exhaust before the burners can light.
limit_switches: Safety switches that shut the burners off if the furnace gets too hot, often from a clogged filter.
blower_wheel: The big fan that moves your home's air through the furnace, the coil and the ducts.
blower_housing: The big fan that moves your home's air through the furnace, the coil and the ducts.
blower_motor: Turns the blower. It runs for heat, for cooling and for fan only.
control_board: The furnace's brain. It runs every step in order and flashes a code light when something is wrong.
furnace_wiring: Carries power and the thermostat's signals.
filter: Catches dust before it reaches the blower and coil. Check it every month or two.
filter_base: Holds the air filter where the return air comes in.
return_platform: The box the furnace stands on. Your home's air comes back through it.
coil_box: Holds the air conditioning coil, on top of the furnace.
coil_door: Holds the air conditioning coil, on top of the furnace.
coil_adapter: Joins the narrower furnace to the wider coil cabinet.
evap_coil: Gets cold when the air conditioner runs. It pulls heat and moisture out of the air going by.
txv: Meters the refrigerant into the cooling coil.
rds_sensor: Watches for a refrigerant leak and turns the blower on to clear it.
drain_cap_aux: Where the water the coil pulls out of the air drains away.
supply_plenum: The box on top where the warm or cool air leaves for your ducts.
warm_air: Your home's air, warmed by the heat exchanger, on its way to the vents.
cool_air: Your home's air on its way through the coil and out to the vents.
return_air: Air coming back from your home to be heated or cooled again.

ac_condenser.title: Air conditioner outdoor unit
ac_condenser.typical: a typical air conditioner outdoor unit

heat.say: Inside your home, the refrigerant soaks up heat from the air. It is pumped out here, where the compressor squeezes it so it gets hotter than the outdoor air. The big fan pulls air in through the coil on the sides and blows that heat out the top. Then the refrigerant goes back inside to pick up more.

lessons.label: Keep the coil clear
lessons.say: The coil wraps around the sides of the unit, and air has to pass through it freely. Keep plants, grass clippings and leaves about two feet away. A dirty or blocked coil makes the unit work harder and cool less.

lessons.label: The power disconnect
lessons.say: The box on the wall near the unit is the power disconnect. Pulling out the block inside cuts the power to the outdoor unit, so it can be worked on safely. Technicians use it before they open the panel.

lessons.label: The capacitor
lessons.say: The capacitor gives the compressor and the fan motor a strong push to get started. It is one of the parts that wears out most often, especially after hot summers. If the fan will not spin or the unit just hums, it is one of the first things a technician checks. It holds a charge, so it is a job for a technician.

base_pan: The metal floor of the unit. The compressor and coil sit on it.
cabinet_posts: The corner posts that hold the unit's sides and top together.
louver_front: The slotted side panels. They protect the coil and let air pass through.
control_panel_cover: Covers the electrical parts in the corner. Only a technician should open it.
data_plate: Lists the model, size and age of the unit.
compressor: The heart of the system. It pumps the refrigerant around and squeezes it so it can give off its heat outdoors.
condenser_coil: Rows of thin metal fins around copper tubing. The heat from your home leaves through here. Keep it clean and clear.
fan: Pulls outdoor air through the coil and blows the heat out the top.
fan_motor: Turns the fan. If the fan stops, the unit cannot get rid of its heat.
fan_grille: The grille on top that keeps hands and debris out of the fan.
top_cap: The top of the cabinet. The fan and its guard sit in it.
orifice_ring: The ring around the fan that helps it pull air through the coil.
capacitor: Gives the compressor and fan motor a strong push to start. A common part to wear out. It holds a charge, so leave it to a technician.
contactor: A switch the thermostat controls. It turns the compressor and fan on and off.
control_box: Holds the electrical parts that start and run the unit.
service_valves: Where the copper lines from the house connect. Technicians check the refrigerant here.
refrigerant_lines: Copper tubing that carries the refrigerant between the compressor, the coil and the house.
disconnect: A box on the wall near the unit. Pulling out the block inside cuts the power to the unit for service.
disconnect_pullout: The removable block inside the disconnect. Out means the unit has no power.
whip: The flexible conduit that brings power from the disconnect to the unit.
pad: The flat base the unit sits on. It keeps the unit level and up off the ground.
heat_stream: The heat taken out of your home leaves here, blown up and away by the fan. Keep a few feet clear above the unit.

heat.say: The blower pulls your home's air in through the filter and across the cooling coil, then pushes it out into the ducts. In summer the coil is cold, so the air leaves cooler and drier. This one lies on its side, a common way to fit an air handler in an attic.

lessons.label: Electric heat
lessons.say: For heat, wire coils at the air outlet glow hot, a lot like a toaster, and the blower pushes your air across them. With a heat pump they help out on the coldest days. They work well but cost more to run than a heat pump.

lessons.label: The filter
lessons.say: The filter catches dust before it reaches the blower and the coil. A clogged filter starves the system of air, so it runs longer, and the coil can even freeze over. Check it every month or two.

lessons.label: Cooling coil
lessons.say: The coil gets cold when the air conditioning runs and pulls heat and moisture out of the air. The water drips into a pan under it and leaves through a drain line. Keeping the filter clean keeps the coil clean too.

cabinet: The metal box of the air handler. The filter, coil, blower and heat strips are all inside.
blower_door: Covers the blower, the controls and the electric heat. Only a technician should open it.
data_plate: Lists the model, size and age of the unit.
insulation: Lines the cabinet so the cold air inside does not sweat on the outside.
supply_flanges: Where the conditioned air leaves the unit for your ducts.
connections: Where the drain lines and the copper refrigerant lines hook up to the unit.
blower_housing: The fan that moves your home's air through the filter, the coil and the ducts.
blower_wheel: Spins to move the air. Dust on its blades cuts the airflow.
blower_motor: Turns the blower wheel. It runs for cooling, for heat and for fan only.
control_board: Runs the blower and the heat when the thermostat asks.
transformer_24v: Turns house power down to the low voltage the thermostat uses.
evap_coil: Gets cold when the air conditioning runs. It pulls heat and moisture out of the air going by.
txv_body: Meters the refrigerant into the cooling coil.
distributor: Splits the refrigerant evenly into the coil's many small tubes.
distributor_feeders: Small tubes that feed refrigerant to each part of the coil.
liquid_line_in: The smaller copper line. It brings refrigerant in from the outdoor unit.
suction_header: The larger copper line. It carries the refrigerant, and the heat it picked up, back outside.
refrigerant_sensor: Watches for a refrigerant leak and turns the blower on to clear it.
heater_kit: Electric heating coils at the air outlet. They warm the air like a toaster.
heater_elements: Electric heating coils at the air outlet. They warm the air like a toaster.
heater_breaker: Turns the power to the heat strips on and off, and trips if something goes wrong.
heater_limit_1: A safety switch that shuts the heat strips off if they get too hot, often from a clogged filter.
sequencer_1: Turns the heat strips on one at a time, so they do not all draw power at once.
filter: Catches dust before it reaches the blower and coil. Check it every month or two.
filter_base: Holds the air filter where your home's air comes back in.
aux_pan: A pan under the unit that catches water if the drain backs up.
rails: Hold the unit up off the attic floor.
supply_air: Your home's air on its way out to the vents.
supply_air_heat: Your home's air, warmed by the heat strips, on its way to the vents.

electric_tankless_water_heater.title: Electric tankless water heater
electric_tankless_water_heater.typical: a typical electric tankless water heater

front_marker.say: the front cover with its display

heat.say: Open a hot tap and a flow sensor feels the water moving. The control board turns on the heating elements, and the water warms as it passes through the heating chambers. It heats only while water flows, so there is no tank to keep hot.

lessons.label: Hard water
lessons.say: In hard water, minerals can coat the inside of the heating chambers. Scale makes the elements run hotter and wear out sooner. Where the water is hard, a technician can flush the heater through its service ports.

lessons.label: The inlet screen
lessons.say: A small screen catches grit where cold water comes in. If your hot water flow drops off, a clogged screen is a common cause. It is a quick rinse.

lessons.label: The power it needs
lessons.say: Heating water the moment you need it takes a lot of electricity. A whole house electric tankless heater often needs heavy wires and two or more large breakers, so your electrical panel has to have room for it.

front_cover: Covers the heating parts and live wiring. Only a trained person should take it off.
chassis: The case that holds the heating chambers and controls.
display_ok: Shows the set temperature. If something is wrong, it shows an error code you can read to your technician.
status_led: Lights up while the heater is heating.
data_plate: Lists the model, power rating and age of the heater.
wall_bracket: Holds the heater on the wall.
heating_chambers: Your water flows through these and warms up on the way through.
heating_elements: Electric coils that heat the water as it passes, like a kettle. They turn on in steps to match how much hot water you use.
thermal_cutoffs: Shut the power off if the chambers ever get too hot.
control_board: The heater's brain. It reads the sensors and sets how much power goes to the elements.
heatsink: Metal fins that keep the control board's power parts cool.
flow_sensor: Feels water moving when you open a hot tap and tells the heater to start.
temperature_sensors: Tell the control board how warm the water is going in and coming out.
junction_box: Where your home's electric lines connect to the heater.
power_feeds: Heavy cables that carry the large current the elements need.
terminal_block: Where the power cables connect inside the heater.
surge_protector: Guards the control board against power surges from storms and the grid.
cold_isolation_valve: Shuts the cold water off to the heater for service.
hot_isolation_valve: Shuts off the hot side for service.
cold_service_port: A side port your technician uses to flush the heater.
hot_service_port: A side port your technician uses to flush the heater.
inlet_filter_screen: A small screen where cold water enters. It catches grit and needs a rinse now and then.
cold_supply_line: Where cold water from your home's supply comes in.
hot_supply_line: Where hot water leaves for your sinks, showers and appliances.
internal_water_lines: Carry your water through the heater.

gas_tankless_water_heater.title: Gas tankless water heater
gas_tankless_water_heater.typical: a typical gas tankless water heater

front_marker.say: the front cover with its display

heat.say: Open a hot tap and water starts flowing through the heater. A fan mixes gas with air and the burner lights. The flame heats coiled tubes with your water running through them, so it comes out hot. There is no tank: it heats only while you use it.

lessons.label: Scale and flushing
lessons.say: Hard water leaves a mineral crust inside the heat exchanger, like the crust in a kettle. Scale slows the heat and can make the heater shut down with an error. A yearly flush through the service valves washes it out.

lessons.label: The condensate drain
lessons.say: This heater uses a second heat exchanger to pull extra heat out of its exhaust. That cools the exhaust so much that water forms, a little like dew. A trap and a drain line carry the water away, so keep that line clear.

lessons.label: Recirculation
lessons.say: Some homes add a small pump that keeps hot water moving through the pipes. Cooled water comes back to the heater on a return line and is heated again, so hot water reaches the far taps sooner. A timer runs it only when you need it.

lessons.label: The inlet screen
lessons.say: A small screen catches grit where cold water comes in. If your hot water flow drops off, a clogged screen is a common cause. It gets rinsed during a flush.

front_cover: The metal cover over the works. Only a trained technician should take it off.
chassis: The metal case that holds the burner, heat exchangers and controls.
display_ok: Shows the water temperature. If something is wrong, it shows an error code you can read to your technician.
data_plate: Lists the model, gas type, size and age of the heater.
burner: Gas and air burn here. The flame turns up or down to match how much hot water you are using.
burner_flame: Burns only while hot water is flowing.
fan_with_venturi: Pulls in air, mixes it with the right amount of gas and pushes the exhaust out the vent.
ignition_unit: Makes the spark that lights the burner.
modulating_gas_valve: Opens a little or a lot so the flame matches the hot water you need.
gas_shutoff_valve: The valve that turns gas off to the heater.
gas_drip_leg: A short capped pipe that catches dirt and moisture before they reach the gas valve.
gas_supply_line: Brings natural gas or propane to the heater.
primary_heat_exchanger: Coiled tubes your water runs through. The flame heats the tubes, and the tubes heat the water.
secondary_heat_exchanger: Catches leftover heat from the exhaust to warm the incoming water. This is what makes the heater so efficient.
hx_scale: A hard mineral crust from hard water. It builds up inside the heat exchanger and slows the heat. A yearly flush keeps it away.
condensate_trap: Collects the water that forms in the exhaust and keeps exhaust gas from escaping out the drain.
condensate_line: Carries that water away to a drain. Keep it clear and free of kinks.
exhaust_vent: Carries the exhaust outside. The exhaust leaves so cool that plastic pipe can be used.
intake_vent: Brings in air for the burner.
air_inlet_filter: Keeps dust and debris out of the burner's air. Your technician cleans it during service.
pc_board: The heater's brain. It watches the sensors and sets the flame.
power_cord: A gas tankless heater still needs electricity to run its fan, igniter and controls.
surge_protector: Guards the control board against power surges from storms and the grid.
pressure_relief_valve: Opens by itself if the water pressure ever gets too high. An important safety part.
prv_discharge: Carries water from the relief valve safely down toward the floor if it ever opens.
cold_isolation_valve: Shuts the cold water off to the heater and has a port your technician uses to flush it.
hot_isolation_valve: Shuts off the hot side and has a port used for flushing.
cold_supply_line: Where cold water from your home's supply comes in.
hot_supply_line: Where hot water leaves for your sinks, showers and appliances.
inlet_filter_screen: A small screen where cold water enters. It catches grit and needs a rinse now and then.
temperature_sensors: Tell the control board how warm the water is going in and coming out.
recirc_pump: Keeps hot water moving through your pipes so it reaches the far taps sooner.
recirc_timer: Runs the pump only at the times you use hot water most, to save energy.
recirc_check: Lets water flow one way only, so the loop never runs backward.
recirc_return: Brings cooled water back from the far end of your pipes to be heated again.

hybrid_water_heater.title: Hybrid water heater
hybrid_water_heater.typical: a typical hybrid heat pump water heater

heat.say: A fan pulls warm air from the room across a cold coil. A compressor, like the one in your refrigerator, moves that heat into the water in the tank. Cooler, drier air blows back out. Electric elements help out when you use a lot of hot water at once.

lessons.label: The air filter
lessons.say: The air filter keeps dust off the cold coil. A dirty filter makes the heat pump work harder and lean on the slower electric elements. Check it and rinse it every few months.

lessons.label: The anode rod
lessons.say: Like any steel tank, this one has a sacrificial anode rod. Over the years it slowly gets eaten away so your tank does not rust. Your technician can check it from the top.

lessons.label: The condensate drain
lessons.say: The cold coil pulls water out of the air, like a glass of ice water sweating on a summer day. That water runs out a drain line. Keep the line clear so it does not back up and spill.

outer_jacket: The metal skin around the tank. Insulation underneath keeps the hot water hot.
data_plate: Lists the model, size and age of the heater.
hp_housing: The top section. It pulls heat out of the room air and puts it into the water.
hp_top: The lid of the heat pump section. Air goes in through the grille here.
hp_front_panel: Covers the heat pump's controls and parts.
air_inlet_grille: Warm room air is drawn in here. Keep the space around the heater open so it can breathe.
air_outlet_grille: Cooler, drier air blows out here. The room near the heater can feel a little cooler.
air_filter: Keeps dust off the cold coil. Rinse it every few months.
compressor: The heart of the heat pump. It moves heat from the air into the water, like a refrigerator in reverse.
evaporator_coil: Gets cold so it can soak up heat from the room air passing over it.
fan: Pulls room air through the filter and across the cold coil.
condensate_drain: Carries away the water the cold coil pulls out of the air. Keep it clear.
electrical_junction_box: Where your home's electric line connects to the heater.
duct_collar: Where an air duct can attach, for installs that bring air in from, or send it to, another space.
anode_rod: A sacrificial metal rod. It slowly corrodes so the steel tank does not. It wears out over the years.
anode_access_cover: A cap on top over the anode rod, so it can be checked and replaced.
upper_heating_element: A backup electric element. It helps heat the top of the tank when demand is high.
lower_heating_element: A backup electric element near the bottom of the tank.
upper_thermostat: Senses the water temperature and controls the upper element.
upper_access_panel: A cover over the upper element and thermostat. Only a trained person should open it: there is live electricity behind it.
lower_access_panel: A cover over the lower element and thermostat. Only a trained person should open it: there is live electricity behind it.
tp_relief_valve: Opens by itself if the tank ever gets too hot or the pressure too high. An important safety part.
tp_discharge_connection: Carries water from the relief valve safely down toward the floor if it ever opens.
drain_valve: Used to flush sediment out of the bottom of the tank.
cold_supply_line: Where cold water from your home's supply comes in.
hot_supply_line: Where hot water leaves for your sinks, showers and appliances.
cold_shutoff_valve: Turns the water off to the heater for service.
hot_shutoff_valve: Closes the hot side for service.
expansion_tank: Gives the water room to grow as it heats, so pressure does not spike in the tank and pipes.
stand: Raises the heater off the floor.

heat.say: The indoor unit pulls room air in through the top, through the filters and across a cold coil. A long fan wheel blows the cooled air back out the bottom, and the vane steers it. Copper lines carry the heat through the wall to the outdoor unit, which blows it outside. Most can also run in reverse to heat in winter.

lessons.label: The filters
lessons.say: Lift the front panel and two mesh filters slide out. Rinse them in the sink and let them dry before they go back. Many makers suggest every few weeks when it runs a lot. Clogged filters cut the airflow and make the unit work harder.

lessons.label: The blower wheel
lessons.say: The long fan wheel and the coil sit in cool, damp air, so dust and mold can build up on them. That can cause a musty smell and weaker airflow. A technician can take the unit apart and deep clean them.

lessons.label: The drain
lessons.say: The coil pulls water out of the air. It drips into a tray and runs out through a drain line that goes through the wall with the copper lines. If that line clogs or does not slope downhill, water can drip from the unit and stain the wall.

front_panel: Lifts up so you can reach the filters.
chassis: The body of the indoor unit. The coil, fan and controls are inside.
intake_grille: Room air comes in through the top here.
filter_left: Two mesh screens that catch dust. Slide them out and rinse them every few weeks when it runs a lot.
coil: Gets cold when cooling, and hot when heating. Your room air passes through it.
blower_wheel: A long fan wheel that blows the air back into the room. Dust and mold on it cut the airflow.
blower_wheel_mold: Dust and mold on the fan wheel. A deep cleaning brings back the airflow.
vane: Swings up and down to steer the air into the room.
louvres: Steer the air left and right.
outlet_throat: Where the conditioned air leaves the unit.
display: Lights that show the unit is on and its mode. Some flash a code when something needs attention.
board: The unit's brain. It reads the remote and runs the fan and the outdoor unit.
drain_stain: Water dripping from the unit, often from a clogged or badly sloped drain line.
back_plate: A metal plate on the wall that the indoor unit hangs on.
air_packets: Room air on its way back out, cooled or warmed.

garbage_disposal.title: Garbage disposal
garbage_disposal.typical: a typical garbage disposal under a kitchen sink

heat.say: Food drops onto a spinning plate at the bottom of the grind chamber. The plate flings it against a rough ring around the edge, which shreds it into tiny bits. Water carries the bits out the side and down the drain. There are no blades inside.

lessons.label: Run cold water
lessons.say: Run cold water before, during and for a few seconds after grinding. The water carries the bits all the way down the drain. Cold water keeps any grease firm so it gets chopped up instead of coating the pipes.

lessons.label: What to keep out
lessons.say: Keep grease, oil, bones, corn husks, celery strings, onion skins, coffee grounds, eggshells, pasta and rice out of the disposal. They tangle, swell or settle and can clog the drain. Small soft scraps with plenty of water are what it is made for.

lessons.label: If it hums or stops
lessons.say: If it hums but does not spin, switch it off first. A hex key in the socket on the bottom turns the motor by hand to free a jam. If it shut itself off, wait a few minutes and press the red reset button on the bottom. Never reach inside.

lessons.label: Dishwasher drain
lessons.say: The dishwasher often drains into the side of the disposal. Its hose loops up high under the counter so dirty sink water cannot run back into the dishwasher. When a new disposal goes in, a small plug inside that inlet has to be knocked out first, or the dishwasher cannot drain.

disposal_body: The motor and grind chamber in one housing, hanging under the sink drain.
disposal_mount: The ring in the sink's drain hole and the mount under it that holds the disposal up. A slow drip here usually means the seal under the sink flange needs redoing.
mount_lower_ring: Twists to lock the disposal onto the mount. Turning it the other way lets the disposal come down.
splash_guard: The rubber flaps in the sink opening. They keep food and spoons from flying out and are easy to replace when torn.
grind_chamber: Where the food is ground. The rough ring around the edge does the shredding.
turntable: Spins fast and throws food against the grind ring. The small lugs on it swing freely. They are not blades.
motor: The electric motor under the grind chamber that spins the plate.
shaft_seal: Keeps water out of the motor. When it wears out, the disposal can leak from the bottom, which usually means it is time for a new one.
reset_button: The red button on the bottom. The motor shuts itself off if it overheats or jams. Wait a few minutes, then press it.
jam_hex: A socket in the middle of the bottom. With the power off, a hex key here turns the motor by hand to free a jam.
discharge_elbow: Where the ground food and water leave the disposal, through a bent pipe into the drain.
disposal_cord: Plugs into the outlet under the sink. Many homes switch that outlet with a wall switch by the sink.
receptacle: The disposal plugs in here. It is often controlled by a wall switch.
dw_hose: Carries the dishwasher's drain water into the disposal. The high loop under the counter keeps sink water out of the dishwasher.
dw_supply: A braided hose that brings hot water to the dishwasher from the shutoff under the sink.
waste_arm: Carries water from the disposal over to the main drain.
waste_tee: Where the disposal's drain and the other sink bowl's drain join together.
p_trap: The curved pipe under the sink. It holds a little water that blocks sewer gas, and catches things before they go down the wall. Its slip nuts loosen so it can come off to clear a clog.
trap_water: The water that always sits in the trap. It is a seal that stops sewer gas from coming up the drain.
strainer_basket: The basket in the other sink bowl. It catches scraps and plugs the drain.
strainer_right: The drain fitting in the other sink bowl, sealed to the sink with gaskets and a big nut underneath.
tailpiece_right: The short straight pipe under the strainer that drops down to the drain tee.
stop_hot: Turns the hot water off to the faucet and, here, the dishwasher too.
stop_cold: Turns the cold water off to the faucet. Good to know where it is before you ever need it.
supply_hot: The flexible hose from the hot shutoff up to the faucet.
supply_cold: The flexible hose from the cold shutoff up to the faucet.
sink: A double bowl sink. The disposal hangs under one bowl.
faucet_pulldown: A pull down kitchen faucet. Run its cold water whenever the disposal is on.
cabinet: The cabinet under the sink. A quick look inside now and then catches small leaks early.
dishwasher: Its drain hose usually connects to the disposal or to the sink drain.

heat.say: Push the handle and the chain lifts the flapper at the bottom of the tank. The tank's water rushes down into the bowl, and the bowl empties through the curved trap like a siphon. The flapper drops shut, and the fill valve refills the tank until the float reaches the set line.

lessons.label: Running toilet
lessons.say: If the flapper no longer seals, tank water slowly slips into the bowl. The level drops until the fill valve turns on by itself to top it up, which is the hiss you may hear at night. A worn flapper is the usual cause and an easy part to replace. A few drops of food coloring in the tank tell you: color in the bowl without a flush means a leak.

lessons.label: Weak flush
lessons.say: If the chain has too much slack, the handle cannot lift the flapper all the way. It drops shut early and the bowl gets only part of the tank. A chain with just a little slack fixes it. A tank water level set too low gives a weak flush too.

lessons.label: Fill valve and float
lessons.say: After a flush the fill valve opens and refills the tank. The float rides up with the water and shuts the valve at the set line. The small refill tube tops up the bowl at the same time, through the overflow tube.

lessons.label: The shutoff
lessons.say: The small valve on the wall behind the toilet turns its water off. Turn it off before working in the tank, or if the bowl is about to overflow. An old or kinked supply line is worth replacing before it leaks.

bowl: The china bowl. A curved trap is molded inside it, out of sight, and carries everything to the drain in the floor.
bowl_water: The water that sits in the bowl seals the drain so sewer gas cannot come up into the room.
trap_flow: The curved channel inside the bowl. During a flush water fills it and pulls the bowl empty, like a siphon.
seat: Bolted to the bowl through two holes at the back.
seat_lid: The cover over the seat and bowl, hinged with the seat.
seat_hinges: Hold the seat and lid on. If the seat shifts side to side, the nuts under the bowl need a snug turn.
tank_shell: Holds the water for the next flush, usually about 1.3 to 1.6 gallons in newer toilets.
tank_lid: Heavy china that cracks if dropped. Set it down on a towel when you take it off.
tank_water: Clean water from your supply line, the same water as your sink. It waits here for the next flush.
handle: Turns the trip lever inside the tank.
trip_lever: The arm inside the tank that lifts the chain when you push the handle.
chain: Connects the trip lever to the flapper. It needs just a little slack: too tight and the flapper leaks, too loose and the flush is weak.
flapper: The rubber seal at the bottom of the tank. It lifts to flush and drops to seal. It wears out over the years and is the most common cause of a running toilet.
flush_valve: The opening the flapper seals, with a tall tube beside it. If the tank ever overfills, water spills down the tube into the bowl instead of onto the floor.
fill_valve: Refills the tank after every flush and shuts off when the float reaches the set line.
refill_tube: A small tube that tops up the bowl water during the refill, through the overflow tube.
float_cup: Rides up with the water and tells the fill valve when to stop. Raising or lowering it sets the tank's water level.
tank_bolts: Hold the tank to the bowl, each with a rubber washer to keep water in.
spud_gasket: The big rubber seal between the tank and the bowl. An old one can leak where the two meet.
angle_stop: Turns the water off to the toilet. Good to know where it is before you ever need it.
supply_line: The short hose that carries water from the shutoff up to the fill valve.
wax_ring: Seals the toilet to the drain in the floor. A toilet that rocks can break this seal, so water or odor may show at the base.
flange: The ring on the drain pipe in the floor. The toilet bolts down to it.
bolt_caps: Two bolts hold the toilet to the flange, hidden under small caps at the base.

water_softener.title: Water softener
water_softener.typical: a typical two tank water softener

heat.say: Hard water comes in at the valve on top and flows down through a bed of tiny resin beads. The beads grab the hardness minerals, calcium and magnesium, and trade them for a little sodium. Soft water rises up the center tube and goes on to your home.

lessons.label: Regeneration
lessons.say: After enough gallons the beads are full and need a wash, usually in the middle of the night. The valve runs water backward through the tank, draws salty brine from the brine tank to clean the beads, rinses them and sends the waste water down the drain. Here you see the backwash step.

lessons.label: Salt bridge
lessons.say: Salt can form a hard crust with an empty space under it, called a salt bridge. The tank looks full, but no salt reaches the water, so the softener stops softening. Push a broom handle down through the salt to break it up, and keep the salt above half full.

lessons.label: The bypass
lessons.say: The bypass valve sends water around the softener, handy when it needs work. While it is on bypass your home gets hard water. If your water seems hard again, check that the bypass was not left turned.

lessons.label: The control
lessons.say: The control keeps the time of day and your water's hardness setting, and counts the gallons used. After a long power outage, check that the clock is right so regeneration still happens at night.

resin_tank: The tall tank. It is filled with tiny resin beads that pull hardness minerals out of the water as it passes through.
valve_head: The valve on top of the resin tank. It steers water through the tank, and runs the cleaning cycle when the beads are full.
control_cover: Shows the time and status. The time of day, your water's hardness and the cleaning time are set here.
control_board: The small circuit board under the cover. It keeps the clock and decides when to regenerate.
display_service: Shows the time of day when the softener is working normally, and the cycle step while it cleans itself.
meter_dome: Counts the gallons that go through, so the softener cleans itself after real use instead of on a fixed calendar.
bypass_valve: Sends water around the softener when it needs work. Left on bypass, your home gets hard water.
inlet_stub: Where water from your home's main line comes into the softener.
outlet_stub: Where softened water leaves for the rest of your home.
drain_line: A small tube that carries the rinse water from each cleaning cycle to a drain.
drain_stub: The drain line should end above the drain with a gap of air, so dirty water can never be pulled back into the softener.
brine_tank: The shorter tank. It holds the salt and the salty water, called brine, used to clean the resin beads.
brine_lid: Lift it to check the salt. A look about once a month is a good habit.
salt_bed: Softener salt slowly dissolves into the water below it to make brine. Keep it above half full and below the top.
salt_bridge: A hard crust of salt with an empty space under it. The tank looks full, but the softener cannot make brine. Break it up with a broom handle.
salt_grid: A platform a few inches up. The salt sits on it and the brine forms underneath.
brine_water: Salty water at the bottom of the tank. The valve draws it up to clean the resin beads.
brine_well: A slotted tube that keeps salt away from the float and the brine line.
brine_float: Shuts off the refill if anything goes wrong, so the brine tank cannot overflow.
brine_line: The small tube between the two tanks. Brine is drawn up through it, and fresh water goes back down it to refill.
wall_transformer: Plugs into a wall outlet and turns house power into low voltage for the control.
power_cord: Carries low voltage power from the adapter to the control.
receptacle: Where the softener's power adapter plugs in.
